duration_source: Complete decode of the specifically approved private Descript export

captions.text: In Core’s left menu, open Deployments.
This workspace keeps a named assignment, its resources, time
reports and expenses together.
Use it for a community support assignment, a search operation, a security
detail or a contractor deployment, as well as fire and E M S work.
The list shows each deployment’s status, finance mode, identifiers and window.
Select New Deployment to prepare a separate fictional
community support exercise.

scenes.title: Choose the purpose, finance mode and contact

captions.text: Give the deployment a recognizable Name.
Choose Finance mode deliberately.
The help explains that Operational only keeps time and expenses for the record,
Cost recovery feeds a reimbursement claim, and Billable feeds a customer invoice.
required_labels: Operational only keeps time and expenses for the record; cost recovery feeds a reimbursement claim; billable feeds a customer invoice.

captions.text: This exercise uses Operational only.
Select the fictional Community Centre as Contact.
Call I D is optional; its help describes one deployment per call.
It stays blank in this example.
Add Notes that explain the assignment and identify the exercise as fictional.

scenes.title: Set the local window and jurisdiction facts

captions.text: Set the Window from November second at eight in the morning to November
fourth at six in the evening.
In Jurisdiction, choose the home and host countries and their state or province.
Both are United States, Illinois here.
Review Time zone and Currency.
The page explains that the accounting time zone belongs to the deployment,
while displayed dates and times use the department’s time zone.
This example retains Central Time and U S D.
Out of province or state and Travel via air remain unchecked
for the local exercise.
Use Agency identifiers for the references supplied for this assignment:
Incident number, Service request number, Resource order number, Request
number, Cost code and Point of hire.
The example uses clearly fictional training references.
These fields help the department relate its deployment record to the
requesting organization’s paperwork.
Select Save, then read the returned details.
The Saved message and Planned badge establish that the deployment exists.
Verify its window, contact, jurisdiction and currency
against the intended assignment.

scenes.title: Reopen and verify the duration settings

captions.text: Use Edit to inspect the stored settings.
The reopened Window retains November second at eight
through November fourth at six.
Max days reads three.
When an end has not been supplied, the maximum-days value helps
define the deployment window used for resource checks; this example
has an explicit end as well.
Check the values before making a later scheduling change.
This visit only verifies what was stored.
Use Cancel to return to the deployment without submitting another edit.

scenes.title: Add the unit and verify its row

captions.text: In Roster, choose the training community van from the unit selector.
Enter C S van one as its Call sign, then select Add unit.
The returned row now lists that vehicle and call sign.
Its Crew value is initially zero because no member has been assigned to it yet.
Adding a unit and adding its people are separate steps.
Check the saved unit row before assigning a member to it.

scenes.title: Assign the member to the saved unit
visual_required_labels: Seat even when a requirement fails

captions.text: Under Personnel, choose Matthew Casey as Member and select the
saved community van as Unit.
This training unit has no configured seat, so Seat and Certification remain blank.
Read the seat help: marked seats require a personnel role, and certification
requirements and expirations are checked.
Keep Seat even when a requirement fails unchecked in this exercise.
required_labels: Seat even when a requirement fails

spoken_references.Seat even when a requirement fails: Seat even when a requirement fails

captions.text: Select Add member.
Verify that Casey appears beside the intended unit and that
its Crew count becomes one.
A unit name alone did not establish that personnel assignment.

scenes.title: Record equipment and verify the complete roster

captions.text: In Equipment, enter Demo radio kit, select the same unit and choose Add equipment.
The saved row now associates the kit with the van.
Its Issued column is a dash in this exercise: this is a free-text
deployment equipment entry, and no inventory issue was performed.
Review the final roster together.
It contains the saved unit and call sign, Casey assigned to
that unit, and the named kit.
Use the stored rows to verify the assignment rather than
relying on a prepared form.

scenes.title: Apply the roster process to your department

captions.text: Use this same prepare, save and verify process for community paramedicine
and mental health response teams, search and rescue, security
companies, wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams.
Fire and E M S departments use the same workspace.
Choose names, contacts, unit assignments and equipment that
fit your organization’s work.
Confirm the people behind the unit count, and keep the deployment’s
identifiers and window useful for the supervisors who will review its work.
